title: Excel Skills Workbook
summary: Multi-tab workbook on a real dataset: data cleaning, lookup and logic formulas, PivotTables, and dashboard charts.
spec: A single .xlsx built from scratch that demonstrates the Excel skills an analyst uses daily, on a realistic pipeline dataset.

list: Data tab — paste the pipeline export and clean it: TRIM/PROPER on names, format dates, remove duplicates. Add a calculated Weighted $ column = Value × Probability (a filled-down formula).

Summary tab — SUMIFS (pipeline $ by stage), COUNTIFS (deals by agent), AVERAGEIFS (avg deal size), and one XLOOKUP (pull an agent's team from a lookup table). Add an IF/IFS column bucketing each deal High / Medium / Low by probability.
PivotTable — weighted pipeline by stage (rows) × agent (columns), plus a PivotChart.
Conditional formatting — color scale on probability, data bars on value, and a rule flagging deals with no activity in 30+ days.
Chart — one clean, titled bar or line chart (pipeline by stage, or deals created per month).

spec: Every number comes from a formula or pivot (nothing hardcoded), the file is tidy, and each tab can be explained in one sentence.

title: Data Quality Case Study
summary: A production data-quality incident I diagnosed and fixed end-to-end — legitimate duplicate charges were being silently dropped from a reconciliation store. Resolved with a schema-enforced per-transaction identity (txn_uid) and a database-level uniqueness invariant.

title: Project Green River
warning: This project examines a real serial-murder cold case (the Green River Killer) and violence against women — the subject is heavy. Ben's perspective comes from a background in law enforcement: the treatment is investigative and clinical, and the victims are treated as real people throughout.
summary: An Azure data-analytics case study that rebuilds a decades-old cold case as a modern cloud data platform. Scattered paper evidence becomes one searchable system — ingested with Data Factory, stored in a Data Lake, analyzed in Synapse with geographic profiling, and acted on through Power BI maps, AI Search, and suspect ranking. The argument: the evidence to identify the killer largely existed by the mid-1980s; what was missing was the ability to organize, search, and connect it — exactly what modern data science provides. It closes by turning the same argument on today's unsolved cases.

title: Direct-Mail Data Pipeline
summary: Turned raw county public-records exports into targeted, compliant real-estate direct-mail campaigns — parsing and USPS-standardizing addresses, building household salutations, deduplicating, and scrubbing against do-not-market lists before handing a clean list to the print vendor (Corefact).

title: Power BI Dashboard
summary: Interactive Power BI report on Closing Day sales data — a modeled star schema, DAX measures, and a recruiter-readable dashboard covering pipeline, GCI, lead source, and geography.
spec: One interactive dashboard built in Power BI Desktop from anonymized Closing Day pipeline data.

list: Export pipeline data to CSV: deals with stage, dollar value, probability, created date, close date, agent, activity counts (names anonymized).
Import to Power BI Desktop and build a simple model (deals table + agents table with a relationship).

Build ONE report page with exactly four visuals: a card row (total pipeline $, weighted pipeline $, deal count, avg deal size), a bar chart (weighted pipeline by stage), a line chart (deals created per month), and a table with conditional formatting on probability.
Add one slicer (by agent or stage) for interactivity.
Save the .pbix and capture 2–3 clean screenshots.

spec: You can open the .pbix, click the slicer, and explain each visual in one sentence. Scope: four visuals, one page — stop there.

title: SQL Analysis Doc
summary: Documented SQL analysis answering real business questions — joins, aggregations, and window functions, with query and result narrative.
spec: A documented set of 15–20 SQL queries against the Closing Day database, each answering a business question.

list: Question in plain English (e.g. "Which stage loses the most deals?").
The query (formatted SQL).
Result (small table or 1–2 lines).
So what — one sentence of business meaning.
Basic SELECT + WHERE filters (2–3).
JOINs across at least two tables (3–4).
GROUP BY with COUNT / SUM / AVG (3–4).
At least one subquery, one CTE (WITH), one window function, and one date-based query.

spec: 15+ entries complete and any one can be rewritten from memory.
